entries.sanskrit:
तृतीये मथुराम् एत्य व्रजात् कंस-वधादिकम् ।

यत् क्र्तं द्वारकायां च कृष्णेन तद् अवर्णयत् ॥

शम् इत्य् अव्ययम् । पित्रोः सुखस्य चिकीर्षयेत्य् अर्थः । तुङ्गाद् राज-मञ्चात् । रिपु-यूथानां नाथं कंसम् । व्यसोर् अपि विकर्षणं पित्रोः सुखार्थम् ॥१॥
word_for_word: the killing of Kaṃsa and the like
and what was done in Dvārakā
with the intention of bringing happiness to His parents
Kaṃsa, lord of the enemy hosts
for the sake of His parents’ happiness
entries.literal_english: In the Third Canto Kṛṣṇa describes what He did after coming from Vraja to Mathurā, including the killing of Kaṃsa, and what He did in Dvārakā. ‘Śam’ is an indeclinable indicating the wish to bring happiness to His parents. He dragged Kaṃsa, lord of the enemy hosts, down from the high royal platform and even dragged the lifeless body, all for His parents’ happiness.

entries.sanskrit: ब्रह्म वेदम् । स-विस्तरं षड्-अङ्गादि-सहितम् । पञ्च-जनोदर-विदारण-द्वारा पुत्रम् आनीयेत्य् अर्थः ॥२॥
word_for_word: with the six limbs and the rest
through tearing open the belly of Pañcajana
entries.literal_english: ‘Brahma’ means the Veda, together with its elaboration, the six limbs and the rest. The meaning is that the son was brought through tearing open the belly of Pañcajana.

entries.sanskrit: भीष्मक-कन्यया रुक्मिण्या ये राजानः समाहूताः । ह्रस्वत्वम् आर्षम् । "समाहृता" इति पाठे आकृष्टा इत्य् अर्थः । केन साधनेन ? श्रियो लक्ष्म्याः स-वर्णेन समानेन रूपेण । यद्यपि तया केवलं श्री-कृष्ण एवाहूतो न सर्वे, तथापि तस्या लावण्यं तेषाम् आगमने हेतुर् इति तयैवाहूता इत्य् उच्यते । एषां मिषतां पश्यतां मूर्ध्नि पदं दधत् । तया सह गान्धर्व-वृत्त्या परस्पर-समय-रूपया बुभूषया भवितुम् इच्छया जहार । कथं-भूतां ? स्व-भागं लक्ष्म्यं शत्वात् । तया स्वात्मनोऽर्पितत्वाच् च । सुपर्णः सुपतनः । यद् वा, सुपर्ण इव स्व-भागं सुधाम् इत्य् अर्थः । यद् वा, श्रियो रुक्मिण्याः समानं वर्ण-द्वयं वाचकं यस्य स श्रियः स-वर्णो रुक्मी, तेन समाहूताः शिशुपालादयः । किम्-अर्थं ? भीष्मक-कन्यया सह तेषां बुभूषया भूतिर् भवत्व् इत्य् एतद् अर्थम् । तत्र शिशुपालस्याह्वानं वरत्वेन बुभूषया, जरासन्धादीनां तद् विवाहोत्सवेन । शेषं पूर्ववत् ॥३॥
word_for_word: the short vowel is an archaic usage
with the reading ‘samāhṛtā’, they were attracted
by a form equal in colour to Śrī Lakṣmī
by her only Śrī Kṛṣṇa was invited
her beauty was the cause of their coming
therefore they are said to have been invited by her
एषाम् मिषताम् पश्यताम् मूर्ध्नि पदम् दधत्
placing His foot upon their heads while they watched
in the form of mutual agreement
with the desire to become [her husband]
knowing her to be His own share of Lakṣmī
because she had offered herself to Him
the invitation of kings such as Rukmī
entries.literal_english: The kings were invited by Rukmiṇī, daughter of Bhīṣmaka. The short vowel is an archaic usage; with the alternate reading ‘samāhṛtā’ they were attracted. The means was her form equal in colour to Śrī Lakṣmī. Although she personally invited only Śrī Kṛṣṇa, her beauty caused the other kings to come, so they too are said to have been invited by her. Kṛṣṇa placed His foot on their heads while they watched and carried Rukmiṇī away by mutual Gandharva consent. She had offered herself to Him and was His own portion of Lakṣmī. Śrīdhara also explains the alternate reading involving Rukmī and the other kings: some desired Rukmiṇī as wife, while others desired the wedding festival.

entries.sanskrit: ककुद्मतो वृषभान् अविद्ध-नासिकान् । विद्ध-नासिकान् कृत्वेति वा । तैर् वृषभैस् तद् दमनेन च भग्नो मानो येषां तथापि तान् गृध्यतः कामयमानान्, अत एवाज्ञान् शस्त्र-भृतो राज्ञस् तच् छस्त्रैर् अक्षत एव जघान ॥४॥
word_for_word: or, having made their noses pierced
He killed them while Himself untouched by their weapons
entries.literal_english: The bulls had humps and unpierced noses—or, according to another reading, their noses were pierced. The pride of the kings was broken by taming those bulls, yet they still desired Rukmiṇī. Therefore Kṛṣṇa killed those ignorant weapon-bearing kings while remaining untouched by their weapons.

entries.sanskrit: यदादित्याः कुण्डले दातुं स्वर्गं गतः, तदा प्रभुः स्वतन्त्रोऽपि ग्राम्यः स्त्री-परतन्त्र इव प्रियायाः सत्यभामायाः प्रियं विधातुम् इच्छुर् द्युतरुं पारिजातम् आनीतवान् । यद्-अर्थे यन्-निमित्तं तं कृष्णं वज्री स्त्री-प्रेरितो योद्धुम् अन्वधावत् । स्व-कार्य-साधकेन तेन युद्धोद्यमस् तस्यायुक्त एवेत्य् आह---क्रीडा-मृग इति । अयं वज्री ॥५॥
word_for_word: when He went to give the earrings to Aditi
like an ordinary man dependent on a woman
desiring to please His beloved Satyabhāmā
He brought the shining Pārijāta tree
for whose sake and on whose account
तम् कृष्णम् वज्री स्त्री-प्रेरितः योद्धुम् अन्वधावत्
Indra, urged by a woman, pursued Kṛṣṇa to fight
entries.literal_english: When Kṛṣṇa went to heaven to give Aditi the earrings, the independent Lord acted like an ordinary man dependent on a woman, wishing to please His beloved Satyabhāmā, and brought the shining Pārijāta tree. Indra, urged by a woman, pursued Kṛṣṇa to fight over it. Since Kṛṣṇa was accomplishing His own purpose, Śrīdhara calls Indra a play-animal.

entries.sanskrit: सुनाभेन चक्रेणोन्मथितः सुतं भौमं दृष्ट्वा तस्य मात्रा धरित्र्या भूम्या आमन्त्रितः प्रार्थितः संस् तस्य तनयाय भगदत्ताय दृत-शेषं राज्यं दत्त्वा ॥६॥
word_for_word: struck down by the Sudarśana discus
entries.literal_english: After Bhauma was struck down by the Sudarśana discus, his mother Earth invited and petitioned Kṛṣṇa. Kṛṣṇa gave the remaining kingdom to Bhauma’s son Bhagadatta.

entries.sanskrit: तत्रान्तः-पुरे कुजेन भौमेन या आहृतास् ताः, प्रहर्षश् च व्रीडा चानुरागश् च तैः प्रहिताः प्रेरिता येऽवलोकास् तैर् जगृहुः स्वीकृतवत्यः ॥७॥
word_for_word: those carried away by the wicked Bhauma
glances impelled by joy, shyness and affection
by those glances they accepted Him
entries.literal_english: The women carried by the wicked Bhauma into the inner quarters accepted Kṛṣṇa through glances impelled by joy, shyness and affection.

entries.sanskrit: आसां योषितां पाणींस् तत्-तद्-अनुरूपः सन् सविधं विवाहोचित-प्रकार-सहितं यथा भवति ॥८॥
word_for_word: together with the fitting marriage procedure
entries.literal_english: Kṛṣṇa took the hands of these women, each in a manner appropriate to her, with the proper procedure suitable for marriage.

entries.sanskrit: सर्वतः सर्वैर् गुणैः स्व-तुल्यानि । प्रकृतेर् मायाया विविधं भवनं विस्तारस् तद्-इच्छया । यद् वा, प्रकृतेर् हितोर् विविधं भवितुम् इच्छया ॥९॥
word_for_word: in every way, with all qualities
the various manifestations of Māyā’s nature
by nature’s desire to become diverse
entries.literal_english: The wives were equal to Kṛṣṇa in every way and in all qualities. The various expansions of Māyā’s nature occur by His will—or, alternatively, by nature’s desire to become diverse.

entries.sanskrit: कालः कालयवनः । रुन्धत आवृण्वतः । मुचुकुन्द-भीमादिभिर् निमित्त-मात्रैः स्वयम् एवाजीघनद् घातितवान् । तेन च स्व-पुंसां तेजः प्रभावं कीर्तिं वा दत्तवान् ॥१०॥
word_for_word: through Muccukunda, Bhīma and the others
He Himself struck down and caused [them] to be killed
तेन च स्व-पुंसाम् तेजः प्रभावम् कीर्तिम् वा दत्तवान्
and thereby gave His own people splendour, power or fame
entries.literal_english: ‘Kāla’ means Kālayavana. Kṛṣṇa restrained and covered the enemy, using Muccukunda, Bhīma and the others as mere instruments; He Himself struck them down or caused them to be killed. Through this He gave His own people splendour, power and fame.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and glossed.

entries.sanskrit: शम्बर-द्विविद-बल्वलान् अन्यान् अपि कांश्चित् प्रद्युम्न-रामादिभिर् घातयद् अघातयत् । "घातयन्" इति वा पाठः । दन्तवक्त्रादीन् स्वयम् अवधीत् ॥११॥
word_for_word: through Pradyumna, Balarāma and the rest
He killed or caused to be killed
or the reading is ‘causing to be killed’
He Himself killed Dantavaktra and the others
entries.literal_english: Śambara, Dvivida, Balvala and certain others were killed or caused to be killed through Pradyumna, Balarāma and the rest; another reading is ‘causing to be killed.’ Kṛṣṇa Himself killed Dantavaktra and the others.

entries.sanskrit: नृपान् घातयद् इत्य् अनुषङ्गः । कथं-भूतान् ? कुरुक्षेत्रम् आपततां गच्छतां येषां बलैः सैन्यैर् भूः सर्वापि चचाल चकम्पे ॥१२॥
word_for_word: the connection is ‘He killed the kings’
the entire earth shook and trembled
entries.literal_english: The sense is connected with the phrase ‘He killed the kings.’ What kind of kings? Those whose forces and armies went to Kurukṣetra and caused the entire earth to shake and tremble.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and glossed.

entries.sanskrit: स कृष्णः । हता श्रीर् आयुश् च यस्य । भग्नाव् ऊरू यस्य तम् उर्व्यां शयानं पश्यन्न् अपि न ननन्द सन्तोषं न प्राप ॥१३॥
word_for_word: whose fortune and life were destroyed
He did not rejoice or attain satisfaction
entries.literal_english: This was Kṛṣṇa. Even seeing the fallen person whose fortune and life had been destroyed and whose thighs were broken, He did not rejoice or become satisfied.

entries.sanskrit: अनभिनन्दन-प्रकारम् एवाह---कियान् इति । द्रोणदिभिर् मूलैः कारण-भूतैः । यद् इति यः अष्टादशाक्षौहिणी-युक्तः । ह्रस्वत्वमार्षम् । क्षपितो य हरुर् भारो भुवः अयं कियान् । अत्य्-अल्प इत्य् अर्थः । यस्मान् मद्-अंशैः प्रद्युम्नादिभिर् हेतु-भूतैर् दुर्विषहं बलम् आस्ते ॥१४॥
word_for_word: he explains the manner of not rejoicing
with Droṇa and the others as root causes
which was accompanied by eighteen akṣauhiṇīs
the burden of the earth that was removed
by My portions beginning with Pradyumna
entries.literal_english: He explains why Kṛṣṇa did not rejoice, asking ‘how much?’ The burden removed from the earth consisted of the eighteen akṣauhiṇīs whose root causes included Droṇa and the others, but how much was actually removed? The answer is: very little, because an unbearable force remained through Kṛṣṇa’s portions, beginning with Pradyumna.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and glossed.

entries.sanskrit: न चात्रान्य उपायः प्रभवति, किन्तु मधुना य आमदः सर्वतो मदस् तेनाताम्र-विलोचनानाम् एषां विवादो यदा भविष्यति, तदा इयान् एवैषां वधोपायः अतोऽन्यो नास्ति । एकात्मानोऽपि मय्य् उद्यते सति स्वयम् एव विवादेनान्तर्दधीरन्न् इत्य् अर्थः ॥१५॥
word_for_word: न च अत्र अन्यः उपायः प्रभवति
no other means is effective here
the quarrel of these red-eyed men
then this alone is the means of killing
they themselves would disappear through quarrelling
entries.literal_english: No other means is effective here. When intoxication produced by honey makes these men red-eyed and they quarrel, that alone becomes the means of killing them. There is no other. Although united as one, when Kṛṣṇa rises against them they will disappear through their own quarrel.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and glossed.

entries.sanskrit: एवं श्लोक-द्वयेनोक्तं क्रमेण सञ्चिन्त्य स्व-राज्ये स्थापयित्वा ॥१६॥
word_for_word: having established [them] in His own kingdom
entries.literal_english: Having successively contemplated what was stated in the two verses, Kṛṣṇa established them in His own kingdom.

entries.sanskrit: साङ्ख्यं प्रकृति-पुरुष-विवेकम् ॥१९॥
entries.literal_english: Sāṅkhya means discrimination between prakṛti and puruṣa.

entries.sanskrit: स्निग्धो यः स्मित-सहितोऽवलोकस् तेन । पीयूष-कल्पया सुधा-तुल्यया । पाठान्तरे सुधा-प्रवाह-रूपया । आत्मना देहेन ॥२०॥ क्षणदया रात्र्या, दत्तः क्षणोऽवसर उत्सवो वा, यासां स्त्रीणां तासु क्षणं सौहृदं यस्य सः ॥२१॥
word_for_word: by the affectionate glance accompanied by a smile
according to another reading, having the form of a stream of nectar
a moment, opportunity or festival was given
He whose affection for them lasted a moment
entries.literal_english: The sweet glance accompanied by a smile was like nectar, or, according to another reading, had the form of a stream of nectar. By His own body, He gave those women a moment, opportunity or festival during the night, and His affection for them was experienced in that moment.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and glossed.

entries.sanskrit: गृह-मेधेषु गृह-धर्मेषु । योगेषु काम-भोगोपायेषु । विराग औदासीन्यं जातम् इत्य् अर्थः ॥२२॥
entries.literal_english: Among householders and household duties, and among the methods for sensual enjoyment, dispassion and indifference arose. That is the meaning.

entries.sanskrit: यदा स्वाधीनेष्व् अपि भगवतो विरागः, तदा दैवाधीनेषु को विस्रम्भेत विश्वासं प्रीतिं वा कुर्यात् ? योगेन चेद् योगेश्वरं श्री-कृष्णम् अनुव्रतः ॥२३॥
word_for_word: when even toward those under His control
कः विस्रम्भेत् विश्वासम् प्रीतिम् वा कुर्यात्
who would place trust, confidence or affection?
one follows Śrī Kṛṣṇa, Lord of yoga
entries.literal_english: If Bhagavān is detached even from those who are under His control, who would place trust, confidence or affection in those who are under the control of fate? If one follows Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of yoga, through yoga, then one has the proper refuge.

entries.sanskrit: शेपुः शापं ददुः । भगवतो मतेऽभिप्राये कोविदाः अभिज्ञाः ॥२४॥
word_for_word: knowing and understanding the Lord’s intention
entries.literal_english: They cursed and gave a curse, knowing and understanding the Lord’s intention.

entries.sanskrit: वयः-शीलादि-बहु-गुणोपेता या गावस् ताः ॥२६॥
word_for_word: cows endowed with many qualities such as age and good nature
entries.literal_english: The cows were endowed with many qualities, such as suitable age and good nature.

entries.sanskrit: कन्याश् च । वृत्ति-करीं जीविका-पर्याप्ताम् ॥२७॥
entries.literal_english: The daughters too were given a livelihood sufficient for their maintenance.

entries.sanskrit: भगवद्-अर्पणं यथा भवति । गो-विप्रार्था असवो येषाम् ॥२८॥
word_for_word: so that it becomes an offering to Bhagavān
whose lives were for the sake of cows and brāhmaṇas
entries.literal_english: The arrangement was made so that it became an offering to Bhagavān; their lives were dedicated to the welfare of cows and brāhmaṇas.
